info.title: lama-caravan admin API
info.description:
The admin API of lama-caravan: the board, its cells, models, clients and cloud accounts. JSON in and out unless an operation says otherwise. A refusal comes back as `{"error": "…"}` with the status the handler chose (400, 401, 403, 404, 409 …), or 500. Some handlers answer a refusal as 200 with `{"ok": false, "error": "…"}` instead; their descriptions say so.

Every route but the public ones needs a session. Before the first account exists only the public ones answer — GET /health says `setupRequired`, and POST /api/auth/setup makes that account. Then POST /api/auth/login `{username, password}` sets the `caravan_session` cookie. A viewer account may call every GET but the raw routes file and log out; everything else needs an admin account (`x-caravan-roles` on each operation). The machine endpoints take the fleet token in `X-Caravan-Token` instead.

Level 1: what each operation does, the query parameters and top-level body fields its code reads, and the content types it answers with. The types of fields and the shapes of answers are not described yet.

post.description:
`routes` is the whole list of the stored clients, each by its `id`: a client left out is removed,
and an id no stored client has is refused — a client is made by `POST /api/consumers/create`, which
gives it its id and key. `routers` replaces the Routing routers and is kept as it is when omitted.
`revision` is the topology's `proxyRevisions.routes` the list was built from: a list built from an
older version is refused with 409 `{error, stale: true, topology}` and nothing is saved, so the page
builds it again from the current topology; without `revision` the save goes through as before. The
proxy service is started if it is down, never restarted; it re-reads the file itself. Answers
`{ok, config, monitor}` with the saved config; 400 for an id named twice, a record with no id or no
`label`, or an id no client has; 500 when the proxy service cannot be started.

post.description:
Send the policy keys (`maxSlots`, `cloudFallbackPct`, `priorityPreemptPct`,
`queueAbortPct`, `preemptGraceSec`, `preemptEnabled`, `stickySlotSec`,
`loadingModelWaitSec`, `queueYieldSec`, `queueLimitSec`, `clientTimeoutSec`, `clientName`) as the body or under
`policy`; keys left out retain their saved values and supplied values are clamped.
`clientName` is the one name every client goes to the cloud providers under, empty for each
client's own (up to 120 printable Latin characters, anything else is refused 400).
All graph queues share `cloudFallbackPct`, `stickySlotSec` and `loadingModelWaitSec`;
obsolete node overrides of these fields are ignored. Every local model's queue
shares `queueYieldSec` — seconds a request waits for a busy model while its pool
has a ready row further on, 0 gives way at once (0–3600, and no more than a limit that
is set: a longer one is cut to it, also when the limit is lowered) — and `queueLimitSec` —
seconds a request waits with nowhere to go before its client is answered 503,
0 is no limit (0–3600). `clientTimeoutSec` is how long a client waits for its whole
answer when its route says none (60–86400, 3600 unless said): the queue's shares are
of it, and each request's record says the moment its client gives up on it
(`clientDeadline`). Queue thresholds are
recalculated in the background afterwards. Answers `{ok, config, monitor}` with the
saved config.

post.description:
`routeId` picks the client; only the fields sent change: `label`, `mode` (open, paused
or drain), `priority` (0-100), `preemptible`, `upstreamType` (llama or cloud; cloud
needs `providerId`), `cloudFallbackProviderId`, the overrides `cloudFallbackPct`,

place of `routeId`, or a key the client would share with another; 409 for a client renamed to the
name another client has (the rule its creation follows).

`port` — a free port for the entry; null or 0 closes it, which is refused while any
client stands: the entry is its only way in. `publicUrl` — the address
consumers are given, e.g. `https://caravan-api.example.org/v1`; the board shows it, the

get.summary: The caravan's own time for one client: medians and 90th percentiles

200.description: The answer. Not described yet: the shape of this value is level 2 of the API description.

schema.description: Not described yet: the shape of this value is level 2 of the API description.

get.description:
`routeId` is the client (400 if it is no id, or a `port` is named in its place); its rows written
before 2026-11-07 under the number it had count as its own. `range` is `1h`, `12h` or
`24h`, anything else covers every day the journal keeps. Read from the finished records'
`latency`, measured since 1.3.437 — older requests are not counted. Answers `{latency}`
with `requests` and, as `{n, p50, p90}` in milliseconds or null when nothing was
measured: `prepMs` (the caravan's own work before the upstream, without the queue),
`connectMs` (opening the upstream connection, 0 when a kept one was taken), `headersMs`
and `firstChunkMs` (the upstream's answer, from the request sent) and `cpuMs` (processor
time of the request). `connReused` is `{n, reused}`: provider requests and how many of
them took a kept connection.

get.summary: Proxy request log of one day, newest first, filterable by client, route, sender or errors

200.description: The answer. Not described yet: the shape of this value is level 2 of the API description.

schema.description: Not described yet: the shape of this value is level 2 of the API description.

get.description:
`date` is YYYY-MM-DD (default: the newest day logged), `limit` caps the rows at
1-2000 (default 200), `since` keeps only the last N minutes of that day, and
`event` (one, or several comma-separated: `finished,blocked`), `routeId` (a client, its
rows written before 2026-11-07 under its old number included), `route` (label substring) and
`client` (the sender's exact IP) filter the rows.
`errors=1` keeps failed requests, `slim=1` drops the bulky queue and active
snapshots, and `summary=1` answers counters per client, by its id — the entry's refusals before a key named
anyone under `entry` — (`routeId`, `total`, `errors`, `byKind`, `topClient`) instead of rows. Answers `{date, dates, rows, limit}` (`dates` lists
the days that have a log); 400 for a malformed `date`, `routeId` or `since`, and for a `port`.

`retrieve` (/v1/models/<id>) on a cloud port, `props` (/props, /v1/props) on a cell's.

get.summary: Talk live with a running cell over its own WebSocket, through the controller

200.description: The answer is sent by code the handler hands the request to; the types listed are only those the handler itself sends. Not described yet: the shape of this value is level 2 of the API description.

get.description:
`cell` names a running cell whose runner talks live (its registry row's `live`:
MiniCPM-o's WebSocket, the protocol of its web demo). Opened as a WebSocket
(`wss://<board>/api/cell-live?cell=…`), the controller opens the cell's own with the
browser's handshake, answers with the cell's 101 and passes the talk on both ways, byte for
byte, until one side ends or both are silent for five minutes; the page may not open a
plain-http cell's WebSocket itself. As a plain GET it answers what a talk would reach:
`{ok, runner, protocol, health: {status, error, ms}}`, the cell's answer to its health said
rather than raised — the window tells a door that drops WebSocket from a cell that is down.
400 for a cell that does not talk live or a handshake that is not a WebSocket's, 404 for no
such machine, 409 for a cell that is not running, 502 when the cell does not answer or does
not open its WebSocket.
